prompts.prompt_text: Harvard has long recognized the importance of enrolling a student body with a diversity of perspectives and experiences. How will the life experiences that shaped who you are today enable you to contribute to Harvard?
Describe a time when you strongly disagreed with someone about an idea or issue. How did you communicate or engage with this person? What did you learn from this experience?
Briefly describe any of your extracurricular activities, employment experience, travel, or family responsibilities that have shaped who you are.
How do you hope to use your Harvard education in the future?
Top 3 things your roommates might like to know about you.

Bowdoin Supplemental Essay (optional): Based on The Offer of the College, which represents Bowdoin's values, you have the option to reflect on any line of The Offer and how it has meaning to you. Which line from The Offer resonates most with you?

Navigating through Differences Essay (optional): Bowdoin believes that its broadly diverse and inclusive campus community prepares graduates to be contributing and useful citizens of the world. Every graduate of this institution should be confident in their preparation to be able to navigate through differences and in all sorts of situations. A Bowdoin education does not guarantee these skills, but it does impart a set of tools necessary to bravely enter unfamiliar conditions with the confidence to deal effectively with ambiguity. If you wish, you may share anything about the unique experiences and perspectives that you would bring with you to the Bowdoin campus and community or an experience you have had that required you to navigate across or through difference.

CMC's mission is to prepare students for thoughtful and productive lives and responsible leadership in business, government, and the professions. With this mission in mind, please explain why you want to attend Claremont McKenna College.

A critical part of fulfilling our mission is living out the commitments of CMC's Open Academy: Freedom of Expression, Viewpoint Diversity, and Constructive Dialogue. We want to learn more about your commitment to listening and learning from others with different viewpoints, perspectives, and life experiences from your own. Describe a time when engaging with someone about a specific topic resulted in you changing your attitude, belief, or behavior, or you changed the belief or behavior of someone else. What was the change that occurred for you, and what facilitated that change? What did you learn from that experience, and how has it informed how you engage with others?

colleges.notes: No supplemental essay required for first-year applicants (2026-27). Application is Common App + a brief 'Panther Profile' of quick questions (not an essay). Creative-talent majors (College of Performing Arts, Dodge College of Film & Media Arts, Department of Art excluding Art History) submit a program-specific Creative Supplement.

prompts.prompt_text: What do you hope to study, and why, at CU Boulder? Or if you don't know quite yet, think about your studies so far, extracurricular/after-school activities, jobs, volunteering, future goals or anything else that has shaped your interests.

(Optional; respond to one of four, 250-500 words) Sarah Lawrence students are often described as hyphenates: filmmaker-sociologist-historian, environmentalist-photographer, psychologist-novelist, economist-poet. In 250-500 words, tell us about seemingly disparate interests you have brought together, or hope to bring together at Sarah Lawrence.

(Optional; respond to one of four, 250-500 words) Students at Sarah Lawrence are asked to design their own research questions directly with faculty, and then answer them through intensive semester-long projects that frequently inspire a blend of intellectual rigor and creativity. In 250-500 words, tell us about a text, problem, or topic you would love to explore over a semester or a year, and what you would hope to achieve through that work.

(Optional; respond to one of four, 250-500 words) Liberal arts and sciences colleges have a long and robust history of providing the educational foundation for the careers of influential politicians, financiers, entrepreneurs, artists, scientists, CEOs, and more. Many of them cite their liberal arts degree as foundational and transformative for how they took on challenges in the world and for shaping their lives after college. How do you see your upcoming college studies leading to your future career (or careers)?

(Optional; respond to one of four, 250-500 words) In today's rapidly changing world, many social, political, and ethical issues spark intense debate and demand nuanced understanding. Choose a contemporary issue that you find both challenging and urgent—whether it relates to identity, justice, artificial intelligence, environment, or another area—and critically explore your perspective on it. How have your previous experiences, background, and/or values shaped your viewpoint? How do you envision engaging with this issue during your college education and beyond?

Catawba essay option (submit one essay of ~250-600 words on one prompt, or answer all three as ~100-250-word short answers): For over 173 years, Catawba College has been recognized for its rich legacy and traditions, sometimes even referred to as a best-kept secret. Could you please share how you first learned about Catawba and what motivated you to apply to our institution?

Catawba essay option (submit one essay of ~250-600 words on one prompt, or answer all three as ~100-250-word short answers): What are your future plans, and why are you interested in the academic program or major you selected? If you are undecided, please share which academic areas you wish to explore at Catawba and why.

Catawba essay option (submit one essay of ~250-600 words on one prompt, or answer all three as ~100-250-word short answers): Catawba is deeply invested in the greater good, cultivating a thriving and livable world for all. Our students, faculty, and staff learn, create, research, explore, and grow. Our good goes far. What "good" do you hope to make at Catawba and beyond?
Why do you want to attend UMass Amherst?
Why did you choose the major you did?
Tell us about a community you are a part of and explain how, as a product of this group or community, you would enrich our campus.
(Commonwealth Honors College applicants) Why do you want to be part of Commonwealth Honors College?
Personal essay (250-650 words; choose a Common Application essay option or respond to one of these UMass Lowell prompts): What do you do in your spare time?

Personal essay (250-650 words; choose a Common Application essay option or respond to one of these UMass Lowell prompts): What is the greatest challenge your generation will face? What ideas do you have for dealing with this issue?
Personal essay (250-650 words; choose a Common Application essay option or respond to one of these UMass Lowell prompts): Formulate the perfect admissions essay question and answer it.

What motivated you to choose your first-choice academic program? In your response, please share personal insights, interests, goals, or experiences—especially those not already included in your application.

colleges.notes: No supplemental essay required for first-year admission as of the 2026-2027 cycle (official UM Admission statement). Apply via the Common App; no UM-specific supplemental essay.

prompts.prompt_text: How did you first learn about the University of San Diego, and what inspired you to apply?

(Choose one of three) USD is committed to fostering a community where everyone feels a sense of belonging and purpose. What does community mean to you and how have you helped create a welcoming environment for others?

(Choose one of three) As a Changemaker Campus, USD challenges students to utilize their learning to actively pursue a more just, sustainable and equitable world. What is a challenge facing humanity today and why does it matter to you?

(Choose one of three) As a contemporary Catholic university, students from all backgrounds and faith traditions are welcomed and celebrated. Share an experience that highlights the ways faith or spirituality–either your own or someone else's–have influenced your life.

Optional Providence College Essay (choose one, 250-500 words): Providence College values each student's willingness to embrace and learn from those with different viewpoints. How will your unique background positively impact others at Providence College?

Optional Providence College Essay (choose one, 250-500 words): Providence College thrives on the energy of those who seek. How will you contribute to our vibrant campus life and intellectual culture in the years ahead?

Optional Nursing Supplemental Essay (Nursing applicants, 150-300 words): Please share more about the experiences, skills, or talents that have led you to want to become a nurse, and how these will contribute to the community at Providence College and to your career as a nurse.
Why Purdue? How will opportunities at Purdue support your interests, both in and out of the classroom?
Why Purdue? Briefly discuss your reasons for choosing your major and your interest in studying at this campus location (Indianapolis or West Lafayette).
The Dickinson Supplement (optional; answer any, all, or none in 50 words or less each): What topic or idea could you write or converse about endlessly?
The Dickinson Supplement (optional; answer any, all, or none in 50 words or less each): What is something new that you'd like to experience, learn or try that might surprise your friends and family?
The Dickinson Supplement (optional; answer any, all, or none in 50 words or less each): What are the qualities that make you proud to be you?

Villanova Writing Supplement (choose one of five, about 250 words): As Pope Leo XIV (Villanova Class of 1977) has said, "no one can single-handedly bear the weight of the challenges the world is facing, just as no one is so weak that they cannot play their part." What have you done to play your part in advancing equity and justice in your community?
Villanova Writing Supplement (choose one of five, about 250 words): What is a lesson in life that you have learned that you would want to share with others at Villanova?
Villanova Writing Supplement (choose one of five, about 250 words): "Villanova" means "new home." Why do you want to call Villanova your new home?

Villanova Writing Supplement (choose one of five, about 250 words): Villanova embraces Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a commitment to thoughtful, ethical use rooted in our Augustinian mission and values. How do you see technology helping you to lead, serve, and contribute to the common good?

Villanova Writing Supplement (choose one of five, about 250 words): At Villanova, we often say "each of us strengthens all of us." Please detail a time when someone has borrowed some of your strength in their time of need.

Tell us why you would like to attend the University of Wisconsin–Madison. In addition, please include why you are interested in studying the major(s) you have selected. If you selected undecided, please describe your areas of possible academic interest.

Each student is unique. Please tell us about the particular life experiences, talents, commitments, and/or interests you will bring to our campus. (Required if applying with the Universities of Wisconsin Application.)

The problems that Harvey Mudd College students hope to tackle are shaped by their experiences, values, and communities. Through our intentionally interdisciplinary curriculum and our mission to develop "a clear understanding of the impact of their work," Mudders develop the skills needed to address these complex challenges and contribute meaningfully to society. Share how an experience you've had or community you belong to has shaped the kinds of problems you want to solve and the impact you want to make.

No one succeeds alone, and at Harvey Mudd College, no one expects you to. In and out of the classroom, HMC students are encouraged to embrace challenges, collaborate with one another, and ask for support when they need it. Describe a time when asking for help made a difference in your work or wellbeing. What led you to reach out, and what did you take away from the experience?

Tell us about a topic or issue that sparks your curiosity and gets you intellectually excited. How do you hope to engage with this topic or issue at Haverford? (Please limit your response to 150-200 words.)

We have highlighted for you some of the values that shape the Haverford community. What are some of the values you seek in your next community? How do Haverford's values, as demonstrated through our Honor Code, resonate with you? As you think about how to answer this question, you might draw from how you have been influenced by other communities you have been a part of, experiences you may have had within your communities, or opportunities you have had to shape or even change your communities. (Please limit your response to 150-200 words.)

Your Space (optional): Your Space is your opportunity to allow the Committee on Admission to learn something about you that you have not addressed in another section of the application. For example, in the past, applicants have shared poetry, short stories, cartoons, digital images of art projects, photography, and collages, and/or links to videos, and short films. It is your space, so if you choose to complete it, send something that is a reflection of you!
Academic Interest Statement: What draws you to the subject(s) you selected as potential major(s)? If undecided, share more about one of your academic passions or interests.
Short-Response Essay (respond to one of the following): Reflecting on a community that you are a part of, what values or perspectives from that community would you bring to Pomona?

Short-Response Essay (respond to one of the following): Describe an experience you had outside the classroom that changed the way you think and/or how you engage with your peers. What was that experience and what did you learn from it?
Short-Response Essay (respond to one of the following): Choose any person or group of people in your life and share how they would describe you.

American University students identify as changemakers and describe themselves as passionate. Describe a belief, hobby, idea, issue, or topic about which you're excited.

Alvernia wants to make sure you've given your application some thought and that you're ready to hit the ground running. Please describe your interest in Alvernia University and how your academic goals fit with our offerings.
Please elaborate on an extracurricular activity, job, or community service initiative that has been particularly meaningful to you and explain why.
After reviewing our institutional mission statement focused on creating a sustainable future and global citizenship, please describe why you are interested in attending Appalachian State.

Tell us about your interest in studying business, including relevant experience or career aspirations, and how Babson can help prepare you to make an impact. (You may respond with a written essay or a one-minute video.)
Share something about your background or viewpoint that speaks to your commitment to promoting understanding across differences or how you will contribute to Babson's collaborative community.
What about being a student at BU most excites you?
Explain your interest in your first-choice major/undecided status and second-choice major, and why you would choose Bucknell University.
Describe your reasons for selecting your intended major, and explain how academic offerings, faculty, or programs at Butler will help you achieve your goals.
Why are you interested in Capitol Technology University? Refer specifically to academic programs, classes, professors, or organizations to show fit for your STEM education.
Why apply to Agnes Scott College? (50–100 words)

Discuss an important global issue and how you would work to address it through SUMMIT. (100 words maximum)
Describe a leader you admire and the influence they have had on you. (5–100 words)

Optional: What is your favorite book that was not assigned in school, and what does it mean to you? (500 characters maximum)
Think about someone you connect with who's different from you. What do you find most meaningful about your interactions with them?
Anything missing? Do you want to share more with us? If so, use this space to fill any gaps you think would assist us in reviewing your application.

How do you define a successful college experience, and how will Carnegie Mellon help you achieve it?
What is something important about your application that you would like to emphasize, or something you haven't yet had the chance to share?
Why Centre? Tell us about the specific academic and community interests that draw you here and how you plan to engage on campus.

Tell us about a time you had an impact on a community, collaborated within one, or were influenced by a community you belong to.

Tell us about your academic interests, your professional goals, and the avenues you hope to explore to reach them.
Why Coastal Carolina?
Elaborate on an extracurricular activity or work experience that has been meaningful to you.
Reflecting on the idea of "Know Thyself," how have you discovered your unique purpose, identity, and goals?
(Honors College applicants) Which descriptor best captures your core identity — creator, doer, explorer, change agent, or seeker? Share examples and how you have developed in that role.

What element on the periodic table best represents you and why?
Why do you want to be an Oredigger? You can share what you want to study, your future involvement and activities, or anything else about the Mines experience that excites you.
What specific aspects of our community and resources excite you, and in what ways are you inspired to contribute to and benefit from our learning community?

What is a challenge facing a community you identify with or care about, and how would your experiences and perspective influence your approach to addressing it?
What encouraged you to apply to Culver-Stockton College in terms of academic programs, campus features, or extracurricular opportunities?
In a single tweet (280 characters maximum), what is your top reason for choosing to apply to D'Youville University?
(Select/custom majors only) If you are applying to a custom or specialized major, what draws you to the field, what are your career aspirations, and how does Drexel's co-op model fit your timeline?
Why does Earlham match your academic style, and how do you plan to contribute to the campus community?
What specific academic programs, campus environments, or strategic opportunities draw you to Elon?
What aspect of your identity do you find most meaningful, and how does it shape who you are?
What three songs make up your perfect playlist, and why do they represent you?
What would be your "Top 5" list on any theme of your choice, and why? (Include a brief explanatory statement.)
What experiences, stories, or professional influences led you to select your intended major or program?

(Optional; choose Option A or Option B) Option B: When have you worked collaboratively with others, and what was that experience like?
